subject: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook
messages:
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook

Team —

Quick context: Aurora Health is ready to start a two-week production pilot on July 6th. They’re a strategic pilot (paying, HIPAA scope) and we committed a 99.9% latency SLA for their go-live window. Their traffic pattern will be bursty (morning batch + steady daytime egress) and the standard dedicated autoscaling policy would likely preempt their burst windows.

Ask: Can we approve a temporary autoscale-exemption + brokered headroom for the pilot (6 GPUs reserved as a soft buffer for 4 weeks), with a clear runbook for failover back to hosted variants? I attached a proposal with utilization projections and a preliminary runbook (pilot-runbook-v1.md).

Constraints I’m aware of: we can’t promise permanent carveouts; Marcus, can you confirm the impact on adjacent pools? Jonas — need ops acceptance on the rollback play and monitoring hooks. Aditya — finance/sales needs a quick note on pricing for the extra buffer.

Goal: greenlight by EOD Friday 2027-06-14 so Aurora can finalize procurement and start onboarding.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270611_aurora_headroom_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-runbook-v1.md (markdown), sla-exception-form.pdf (pdf)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook

Kim —

I reviewed the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can provision a 6-GPU soft buffer for four weeks, but it will require bumping the allocation of one pilot tranche (the eval-slate pool) by 30% and tightening preemption thresholds on two low-priority internal queues. Net effect: ~12% reduction in immediate burst capacity for non-paying trials for that period.

Operational caveats:
- We should label the reserved GPUs as "brokered-pilot/aurora-2027" for tracing and billing.
- We need an explicit eviction grace of 90s (vs our default 30s) to avoid mid-request OOMs when we shift capacity.

I can make the config changes but need signoff from Ops (Jonas) and Product (Kim) for the eviction grace increase. Also flagging that this will increase token costs for Aurora’s pilot; Laura, can we surface pricing?

Marcus
Sr Product Mgr, Dedicated

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook

Marcus/Team —

Ops accepts in principle but with two operational controls before we flip the switch:
1) Automated rollback trigger: if pod saturation > 85% for 3 consecutive 5-min windows, revert brokered headroom and route traffic to hosted fallback (model variant x-small).
2) Monitoring: add per-tenant token-latency SLO dashboard + an alert that pages on-call if average p50 latency > 450ms for 10 minutes.

I also want the runbook to include exact steps for: drain, failover, customer notification cadence, and a postmortem template. I reviewed pilot-runbook-v1.md and left inline comments in Drive.

Once we have those pieces, Ops can schedule the capacity change for a Tuesday maintenance window (preferred) or do a hot change for the pilot start if business requires it.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Ops
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook

Kim —

Laura from Revenue Ops here. Proposed pricing for the 4-week buffer (6 GPUs, brokered label):
- One-time setup & ops coordination fee: $6,000
- Temporary headroom usage (weekly): $2,500/week (billed at end of pilot)
- If Aurora exceeds 75% of buffered capacity for more than 3 days, we convert to a short-term reserved tranche at a discounted rate (TBD).

I’ll draft a short amendment to the existing MSA (DocuSign-ready) — need legal to fast-track. Aditya please confirm whether we can absorb the setup fee into a pilot rebate if we want to sweeten the deal.

Laura Bennett
Revenue Operations
From: sara@aurorahealth.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2027-06-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brokered headroom for Aurora pilot — temporary SLA exception & runbook

Thanks Kim & team —

This looks good from Aurora’s side. We can accept the eviction grace and the automated rollback trigger; our onboarding team prefers the Tuesday maintenance window but we could make an exception for an earlier hot change if needed. Two clarifications from us:
1) Can you add a short note in the runbook that our site-contact (ops@aurorahealth.com) will be notified immediately when the rollback trigger fires?
2) Does the brokered label allow us to see usage in the console (per-tenant breakdown) or will we rely on weekly reports?

If you can confirm these two items and send the DocuSign amendment, we’ll sign and greenlight procurement tomorrow.

—Sara Ellis
Product Operations, Aurora Health
